about: Our own answer key: 47 new questions, each labelled against the ten assignment questions in corpus.json. The assignment's ten questions contain no hard cases, so these add them: copies with different formatting, same questions in very different words, number swaps, and look-alike questions that test something else. Labels were fixed before any judge saw them; see 'audit'.
rule: Perfect-answer test (decision D7): two questions are the same if a perfect answer to one would earn full marks on the other. Compare the concept and the task.

labels.exact_duplicate: the same text once case, punctuation, spacing and list or formatting marks are ignored
labels.semantic_duplicate: different words or format, same concept and same task; also a question made only by joining existing questions together
labels.variant: same concept and same task; only the numbers change (decision D8)
labels.different: a different concept, or the same concept with a different task
labels.needs_review: broader, narrower or looser than an existing question, so the answer depends on context (decision D9)

fields.of: the corpus question or questions this candidate relates to; any question in the same duplicate group counts as a correct match. Two entries mean the candidate joins two existing questions
fields.looks_like: for 'different' candidates, the corpus question it resembles on the surface
fields.judgement_call: true where a careful person could reasonably choose another label
fields.added: set on questions written after the first judge tests (2026-10-15 audit); results for them are reported separately

audit.why_removed: redundant with another test question, off the subject, or worded like the judge's own examples. None of the removed questions was answered wrongly by any judge, so removing them can only lower the scores, not raise them.
audit.added_because: only 3 variant and 3 needs-review questions existed, too few to measure those cases
